description: Issue #931 item 6 (cross-vendor review of #923): every OTHER test in this file that exercises the Development ephemeral-key path (AddWtmAuthentication_DevelopmentEphemeralKey_IsWiredIntoBothConfigsObjectGraphs, the two code-delegate tests, etc.) only asserts that SOME 32+-byte key was generated and wired consistently into both the config.Get<Configs>() snapshot and IOptionsMonitor<Configs> -- none of them binds to the key actually being unpredictable. Replacing FrameworkServiceExtension.AddWtmAuthentication's `RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32)` (a CSPRNG call) with `new byte[32]` (a deterministic, all-zero, entirely predictable array) would satisfy every one of those tests: the resulting Base64 string is still 32+ raw bytes, still not one of JwtOption.KnownPublicKeys, still gets wired into both object graphs identically -- but every process, every restart, every deployment would generate the IDENTICAL signing key, which is exactly as forgeable as a hardcoded one once it leaks (and 'the same base64 string every time this exact code path runs' is trivially guessable without any leak at all). This mutant reintroduces exactly that: `Convert.ToBase64String(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32))` becomes `Convert.ToBase64String(new byte[32])`. The red test calls AddWtmAuthentication.CurrentValue.JwtOptions.SecurityKey from two INDEPENDENT ServiceCollection instances (no shared state) and asserts the two generated keys differ from each other and from the all-zero constant's own Base64 form -- under the mutant both independent calls produce the identical all-zero-derived string, failing both AreNotEqual assertions.
target_symbol: AddWtmAuthentication -- the `var generatedKey = Convert.ToBase64String(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32));` line inside the Development ephemeral-key branch, which must call the CSPRNG, not construct a zero-filled array
